children: ConvaTec Group shares surged after the medical products company raised its revenue growth forecast for the year, citing accelerating growth in the second half.
London-listed shares were up 9.2% at 269.60 pence on Wednesday morning, leading the FTSE 100 index, which was trading 0.2% lower.
The company said it now expects 2026 organic revenue growth excluding  InnovaMatrix at between 6.25% and 7.0%, up from previous guidance of between 5.5% and 6.5%.
Organic revenue excluding InnovaMatrix climbed 6.6% in the 10 months through October. Reported revenue growth was 4.8%, while total organic growth for the period was 3.7%.
ConvaTec said it saw stronger growth in the second half in its infusion care and continence care businesses.

"Revenue growth has accelerated in the second half, as we expected...Overall, we continued to gain share in all categories, underpinned by new product launches," Chief Executive Officer Jonny Mason said.

The company reiterated its 2026 adjusted operating profit margin and adjusted earnings-per-share guidance. It expects an adjusted operating profit margin of at least 23% with double-digit growth in adjusted earnings per share.
ConvaTec also reiterated its medium-term targets for between 6% and 8% organic revenue growth driving a double-digit rise in adjusted EPS.

"Heading into the results, there have been ongoing concerns around the [second-half] step up required to meet the [2026] guidance and today's upgraded top-line and reiterated margin guidance...should put those worries at ease," J.P. Morgan analysts said.
